title: Errors and irregularities in bank transactions remain undetected
description: Unrecorded bank charges, direct debits, errors, or misappropriation through the bank account are not identified because the reconciliation is not subject to independent scrutiny.
causes: No independent review of reconciliations; reconciliations prepared late or not at all; long-outstanding items never investigated; preparer also handles cash.
misstatement_scenario: Cash balance misstated; unrecorded liabilities or expenses (bank charges, automatic payments); fraud through the bank account concealed by stale reconciling items.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with transaction volume, the number of automatic bank transactions, and where the preparer handles cash. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists - it is a control deficiency creating detection risk, and the balance must be tested.

title: Unauthorised or fraudulent payments to unfamiliar beneficiaries
description: Funds are disbursed to fictitious or improper beneficiaries, whether through falsified supporting documents, diverted supplier payments, or payments with no business purpose.
causes: No verification of new beneficiaries; weak payment approval; beneficiary master data uncontrolled; supporting documents fabricated or absent.
misstatement_scenario: Cash misappropriated; expenses overstated or misclassified to conceal the payments; duplicate payments diverted to unauthorised accounts.
inherent_risk_factors:
Risk increases with payment volumes, electronic payment files, and weak beneficiary controls. Unusual payments are indicators to investigate; they do NOT prove that fraud has occurred.

Significance: Significant risk

title: Cash misstated through year-end transfer cut-off errors
description: Transfers recorded as received before year-end but not yet dispatched (or vice versa) double-count or omit cash, overstating or understating the reported balance - whether by error or deliberate window dressing.
causes: Timing differences not properly accounted for; transfers recorded on the receiving side only; deliberate inflation of the reported cash balance.
misstatement_scenario: Cash overstated through double-counting in transit; misleading liquidity position presented; compensating errors conceal the true position.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with the value of transfers in the cut-off window and with pressure to present a strong liquidity position. The factor creates cut-off risk to be tested; it does NOT prove the cash balance is misstated.

title: Cash on hand misappropriated or misstated
description: Physical cash is removed or lost without detection, and the recorded balance exceeds cash actually held.
causes: No independent counts; single custody of cash; IOUs treated as cash; weak receipting of cash received.
misstatement_scenario: Cash overstated; losses concealed within the balance; a weak cash control environment signalling wider control issues.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with the volume of cash handled and the number of people with access. The absence of verification does NOT prove any shortage exists - existence must be tested directly.

title: Fraudulent financial reporting through manual journal manipulation (management override)
description: Management or staff use manual journal entries - particularly at period-end, outside hours, or through seldom-used accounts - to misstate reported results, bypassing the controls that govern routine transactions.
causes: Management override of controls; ability to post journals outside normal processes; weak independent review of period-end entries.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue, expenses, assets or liabilities misstated through fictitious or reclassified journals; results shifted between periods; audit trail obscured.
inherent_risk_factors:
Fraud risk indicators, including those in this library, are red flags that require investigation. They do NOT prove that fraud has occurred, and most indicators have innocent explanations. The auditor's response is extended procedures and scepticism, not accusation.

Significance: Significant risk

title: Misappropriation of assets concealed by falsified records
description: Assets - cash, inventory or other resources - are stolen or diverted for personal use, and the accounting records are falsified to conceal the diversion.
causes: Opportunity created by weak segregation of duties, poor physical controls over assets, and inadequate independent reconciliation.
misstatement_scenario: Assets overstated (diverted assets still carried, or fictitious assets recorded); losses unrecorded; expenses inflated to absorb the diversion.
inherent_risk_factors:
Fraud risk indicators are red flags that require investigation. They do NOT prove that fraud has occurred, and most indicators have innocent explanations. The auditor's response is extended procedures and scepticism, not accusation.

Significance: Significant risk

title: Fictitious or premature revenue to meet targets
description: Revenue is recorded for transactions that did not occur, or genuine revenue is recognised before the applicable recognition criteria are satisfied, in order to meet targets.
causes: Intense pressure to meet revenue targets, bonus thresholds, forecasts or covenants; weak cut-off controls; sales team incentives misaligned with proper recognition.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue and receivables overstated; profit inflated; subsequent periods correspondingly understated when the premature amounts reverse.
inherent_risk_factors:
Fraud risk indicators are red flags that require investigation. They do NOT prove that fraud has occurred, and most indicators have innocent explanations. The auditor's response is extended procedures and scepticism, not accusation.

Significance: Significant risk

title: Systematic management bias in accounting estimates
description: Management's assumptions in significant accounting estimates are systematically skewed in the direction favourable to reported results - individually within a plausible range, but collectively one-sided.
causes: Pressure to report desired results combined with the subjectivity inherent in estimates; weak independent challenge of assumptions.
misstatement_scenario: Carrying amounts misstated (provisions understated, impairments avoided, fair values inflated); profit smoothed or inflated across periods.
inherent_risk_factors:
Fraud risk indicators are red flags that require investigation. They do NOT prove that fraud has occurred, and most indicators have innocent explanations. An optimistic estimate is not evidence of dishonest intent; only a pattern, combined with other evidence, warrants escalation.

Significance: Significant risk

title: Unsupported manual journal entries misstate the financial statements
description: Manual journal entries may be invalid, inaccurate or unsupported, and the absence of documentation means the auditor cannot vouch them to genuine underlying transactions or events. Period-end journals are particularly susceptible because of the pressure to close and the opportunity to adjust reported results.
causes: Period-end time pressure; weak journal approval discipline; preparers who do not understand what constitutes adequate support; deliberate omission of support to conceal inappropriate entries.
misstatement_scenario: Account balances and transaction totals may be misstated by invalid or inaccurate journals. Errors and irregularities may be concealed within unsupported adjustments. The financial statements may reflect management's desired outcome rather than underlying performance.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with the volume of manual journals, the extent of period-end adjustment, and the seniority of those posting. An unsupported journal is an exception - a failure of evidence - and a cluster of unsupported period-end journals is a suspected fraud indicator. Neither proves that a misstatement exists; each must be investigated on its own evidence, and fraud must never be concluded from the absence of support alone.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Fraudulent financial reporting through management override of controls
description: Management may override controls that would otherwise operate effectively - posting journals directly, directing staff to process inappropriate entries, or adjusting records outside the normal process - in order to misstate the financial statements. Override is by nature unpredictable and can affect any account or disclosure.
causes: Concentration of authority in senior management; weak or dominated governance; broad privileged system access; performance pressure combined with opportunity; a culture in which challenge is discouraged.
misstatement_scenario: Material misstatement anywhere in the financial statements, including through fictitious journals, biased estimates, or concealed transactions. Normal controls provide no protection against override, so the auditor's response must be specifically designed for it.
inherent_risk_factors: The factor describes opportunity, not occurrence: the ability to override does not prove that override has happened. Throughout the work the auditor must distinguish the risk factor (opportunity exists), the identified risk (override could cause material misstatement), a suspected fraud indicator (something actually looks wrong), and confirmed fraud (proven). A failed test in this area raises the assessed risk; it does not by itself prove fraud.

title: Undisclosed or improperly measured related-party transactions
description: Transactions with related parties may occur at non-arm's-length terms, lack commercial substance, or remain entirely undisclosed, because no process identifies the relationships in the first place. Both measurement and disclosure may then be wrong.
causes: Complex or opaque group and ownership structures; directors with undisclosed outside interests; no assigned responsibility for maintaining related-party information; transactions deliberately structured to obscure the relationship.
misstatement_scenario: Related-party disclosures may be incomplete or misleading. Transactions may be measured on terms that do not reflect their substance. Users may be unaware of relationships that affect their assessment of the entity.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with structural complexity and with the volume of transactions lacking obvious commercial logic. The missing identification process is a control deficiency; any particular undisclosed transaction is a potential misstatement to be investigated. The presence of this factor does not prove that undisclosed related-party transactions exist.
source_ref: audit-risk-library v1.2 (2026-10-22); Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

title: Materially misstated provisions from unsupported assumptions
description: Provisions may be materially over- or understated, or required provisions omitted entirely, because the assumptions underlying them are undocumented, unsupported by evidence, or never independently challenged.
causes: Genuine estimation uncertainty combined with inadequate discipline; management optimism or pessimism; reluctance to obtain external advice; assumptions carried forward without re-examination; earnings-management incentives.
misstatement_scenario: Liabilities may be materially misstated, affecting profit, net assets and key ratios. Estimation uncertainty may not be disclosed. A pattern of one-sided assumptions may indicate bias, which is a fraud risk factor.
inherent_risk_factors: Estimation uncertainty is inherent in provisions; the risk here is the absence of the support and challenge that would keep estimates honest. An unsupported assumption is a deficiency in evidence, not proof the provision is wrong - the auditor must develop an independent expectation. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Incomplete or inadequate financial statement disclosures
description: Financial statements may omit disclosures required by the applicable financial reporting framework, or present outdated or unclear disclosures, because no checklist or technical review ensures completeness. The primary statements may balance perfectly while the notes mislead by omission.
causes: No assigned responsibility for disclosures; prior-year notes rolled forward without updating; new standards or transactions not assessed; preparers focused on the trial balance rather than the notes.
misstatement_scenario: Users may lack information material to their decisions - about risks, uncertainties, related parties, or subsequent events. The financial statements taken as a whole may be misleading despite accurate primary statements.
inherent_risk_factors: An omitted disclosure does not affect any account balance, which is why the risk is easily overlooked. The factor is a control gap in the reporting process; whether any particular omission is material requires judgment. The presence of this factor does not prove that required disclosures are missing.

title: Decommissioning provision omitted or understated; related asset-retirement cost not capitalised
description: The entity may fail to recognise a provision for dismantling and restoring leased network sites, or measure it using unsupported cost or discount assumptions. The related decommissioning cost that should be capitalised as part of the asset may be omitted.
causes: Thousands of dispersed sites make the obligation easy to overlook; restoration cost estimates rely on management assumptions about timing, cost and discount rates; unwinding of discount is sometimes missed.
misstatement_scenario: Provisions may be understated or missing entirely, understating liabilities. Property, plant and equipment may be understated where the capitalised decommissioning cost is omitted, with a corresponding understatement of depreciation.
inherent_risk_factors:
Decommissioning measurement is inherently judgmental and the number of sites magnifies small per-site errors. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

Significance: Significant risk

title: Incorrect allocation of consideration across bundle components and premature revenue recognition
description: Consideration may be allocated using unsupported stand-alone selling prices, or recognised before the related service is delivered, accelerating revenue into earlier periods.
causes: Allocation requires judgment about stand-alone selling prices; high transaction volumes are processed by automated rating engines whose configuration is rarely re-tested; promotions change frequently.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue may be overstated in early periods and understated later; equipment and service revenue may be misclassified between lines.
inherent_risk_factors: Complexity and volume magnify small systematic allocation errors. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Systematic billing errors from rating or tariff configuration
description: A misconfigured tariff, discount or rating rule is applied to every affected transaction until detected, producing systematic over- or under-billing across the subscriber base.
causes: Error is systematic: one defect affects thousands of records identically. Detection depends on exception monitoring and reconciliation, which may be weak.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue may be materially misstated in either direction; related receivables and deferred revenue are affected in the same direction.
inherent_risk_factors: Automation concentrates risk in configuration rather than individual transactions. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Misallocated overheads and misstated work in progress
description: Overhead rates may be based on outdated budgets, normal capacity may be overstated (absorbing abnormal idle costs), or allocation bases may not reflect actual consumption - misstating WIP and cost of sales.
causes: Overhead absorption is an estimate built on estimates; idle-capacity treatment requires judgment; WIP is harder to verify physically than finished goods.
misstatement_scenario: Inventory (WIP) may be overstated with a corresponding understatement of cost of sales; or understated where rates lag actual costs.
inherent_risk_factors: Judgment concentrates in the rate-setting and capacity assumptions. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Variances buried rather than analysed, misstating inventory and cost of sales
description: Material variances may indicate that standards are outdated (misstating inventory) or that real inefficiencies, waste or price changes are being hidden in cost of sales without investigation.
causes: Variances are the system's own diagnostic signal; ignoring them removes the detective control the system was designed to provide.
misstatement_scenario: Inventory may be misstated where standards no longer reflect actual costs; cost of sales absorbs unexplained amounts.
inherent_risk_factors: The variance pattern is evidence to investigate, not a conclusion. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Understated warranty provision
description: The provision may be based on outdated failure rates, ignore new-product risk, or simply not be updated for actual claim experience - understating liabilities.
causes: Measurement relies on historical claim rates that may not predict new products; management has an incentive to minimise the charge.
misstatement_scenario: Liabilities understated; expenses understated in the period of sale.
inherent_risk_factors: Estimation uncertainty is the core risk, highest for new products. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Unrecorded sales and theft of takings (shrinkage)
description: Cash sales may be skimmed before recording, voids and refunds may be fictitious, and shrinkage may go unrecorded - understating revenue and overstating the resulting loss only when discovered.
causes: Cash is the most stealable asset and high volumes hide small diversions; detection depends on reconciliations that may be perfunctory.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue understated (skimmed sales never recorded); cash understated; shrinkage losses unrecorded until count.
inherent_risk_factors:
Volume provides cover for small, repeated diversions. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement or theft exists.

Significance: Significant risk

title: Premature or overstated recognition of supplier rebates
description: Rebate income may be recognised before the qualifying purchase volumes are achieved, or accrued on terms the supplier has not agreed - overstating income and receivables.
causes: Recognition depends on future volumes and supplier confirmation, both uncertain at the reporting date; commercial pressure favours optimism.
misstatement_scenario: Other income and rebate receivables overstated; recognised in the wrong period.
inherent_risk_factors: Rebates reward optimism: the estimate almost always favours the retailer. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Understated deferred revenue from unredeemed gift cards and loyalty points
description: Liabilities for unredeemed cards and points may be released prematurely, or breakage recognised aggressively - understating deferred revenue and overstating current revenue.
causes: Redemption patterns are behavioural estimates; breakage is invisible until enough time passes; the liability is a prime target for earnings management.
misstatement_scenario: Deferred revenue understated; revenue overstated in the current period.
inherent_risk_factors: Breakage is estimated, not observed, at the reporting date. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Understated loan impairment (expected credit losses)
description: Staging may be optimistic, model parameters stale, forward-looking scenarios benign, or overlays used to suppress the charge - understating impairment and overstating the loan book.
causes: ECL is the most judgmental number in a bank: it combines models, staging judgments and economic forecasts, each of which can be tilted.
misstatement_scenario: Loans overstated; impairment charge understated; disclosures may hide the sensitivity.
inherent_risk_factors:
Model risk and staging judgment dominate. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

Significance: Significant risk

title: Overstated interest income on non-performing loans
description: Interest accrued on doubtful loans may never be collected; without suspension or adequate provision against the accrued interest, income and receivables are overstated.
causes: Accrual is automatic; stopping it requires an active decision that may be delayed for performance reasons.
misstatement_scenario: Interest income overstated; loan receivables overstated to the extent accrued interest is unprovided.
inherent_risk_factors: The policy boundary for suspension is the key judgment. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Misclassification and valuation error in financial instruments
description: Instruments may be classified to achieve a desired measurement outcome, and model valuations may use optimistic inputs - misstating assets, liabilities and profit or loss.
causes: Valuation models are complex and their inputs partly unobservable, creating information asymmetry between management and the auditor.
misstatement_scenario: Financial assets/liabilities misstated; gains or losses recognised in the wrong period or the wrong statement section.
inherent_risk_factors: Model complexity is the risk multiplier. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Inventory loss through theft, unauthorised removal or unrecorded damage
description: Inventory may be stolen, lost or removed without authorisation, or damaged without the loss being recorded. If such losses are not identified and recorded, inventory quantities in the accounting records will exceed quantities actually held.
causes: Unrestricted physical access to storage areas; absence of segregation between custody of inventory and record-keeping; weak or unenforced goods movement procedures; collusion or opportunistic theft.
misstatement_scenario: Inventory may be overstated if losses are not recorded. Inventory records may not agree with physical quantities. Losses may be incorrectly classified or omitted from the accounts.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with the portability and resale value of inventory, the number of people with access, and the absence of perpetual records. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Payments to ghost or terminated employees
description: Wages, allowances or termination-related payments continue to be processed for individuals who have left employment, diverting funds and overstating payroll costs.
causes: Leaver notifications not communicated from HR to payroll; no periodic reconciliation between the payroll master and HR employment records; bulk electronic payments processed without payee-by-payee review.
misstatement_scenario: Payroll costs and related liabilities are overstated; cash is diverted to unauthorised recipients; statutory deductions on ghost pay may create compliance issues.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with payroll size, staff turnover and electronic bulk payments. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists - it identifies a possibility the auditor must test, not a finding.

title: Fictitious employees created or pay details manipulated
description: An individual with combined custody of employee records and payments could create fictitious employees, inflate pay rates, alter bank details, or process duplicate payments, diverting cash.
causes: No segregation of duties between master maintenance and payment processing; excessive system access rights; no independent approval of master changes; no review of the payroll payment file before release.
misstatement_scenario: Payroll expense overstated; cash diverted to unauthorised recipients; bank detail changes misdirect legitimate pay.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases where one person has end-to-end control and where payments are released without review. The factor describes a control deficiency that creates opportunity; it does NOT prove that fraud or misstatement has occurred.

title: Inflated or fictitious overtime payments
description: Employees may claim overtime not worked, or record excessive hours, and the amounts are paid without detection, overstating payroll costs.
causes: No independent approval of overtime; self-reported timesheets; no comparison of overtime to production or attendance records.
misstatement_scenario: Payroll costs overstated; inequitable or fraudulent payments; budget overruns in labour-intensive operations.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases where overtime is material, paid at premium rates, and self-reported. The absence of approval does NOT prove any claim was inflated - each claim must be tested.

title: Payroll expense and deductions misstated through calculation errors
description: Systematic or isolated errors in pay rates, tax calculations or deductions cause wages, tax liabilities and related balances to be misstated.
causes: Outdated tax tables; manual rate entry errors; incorrect payroll system configuration; unauthorised rate changes.
misstatement_scenario: Wages expense misstated; statutory liabilities (tax, social security) misstated with compliance consequences; employee relations issues.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with manual processing, frequent rate changes and complex deductions. Identifying this factor means calculation accuracy must be tested; it does NOT prove that any specific payment is wrong.

title: Inappropriate capitalisation of repairs and maintenance expenditure
description: Revenue expenditure on repairs and maintenance may be capitalised as property, plant and equipment even though it does not meet the recognition criteria for an asset. The result is overstated assets and understated expenses for the period, with overstated depreciation in future periods.
causes: Judgment involved in distinguishing repairs from improvements; pressure to report higher profits by deferring expense recognition; absence of a documented capitalisation policy or inconsistent application; approval processes that address budget but not accounting treatment.
misstatement_scenario: Property, plant and equipment may be overstated. Profit for the period may be overstated because expenses are understated. Future depreciation charges will be overstated.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with the volume of expenditure near the capitalisation boundary, the complexity of the asset base, and where performance measures reward reported profit. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; it identifies where the auditor should direct attention and professional skepticism.

title: Incorrect depreciation charges and carrying amounts
description: Depreciation may be understated or overstated, and the carrying amount of property, plant and equipment misstated, because the rates, methods or useful lives applied do not reflect the expected pattern of consumption of the assets' future economic benefits.
causes: Depreciation parameters set at initial recognition and never revisited; changes in asset usage, technology or condition not reflected; deliberate extension of useful lives to reduce the charge; errors in the asset register.
misstatement_scenario: The depreciation charge for the period may be materially misstated. The carrying amount of property, plant and equipment may not reflect the consumption of economic benefits. Changes in estimates may be applied incorrectly (retrospectively instead of prospectively).
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with the age and technological sensitivity of the asset base and where small changes in lives have a material effect on profit. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; the current parameters may still happen to be reasonable, which is what the auditor must evaluate.

title: Disposed assets remain recognised in the accounting records
description: Assets that have been sold, scrapped, demolished or otherwise disposed of may continue to be recognised in the fixed asset register and the general ledger. The existence assertion for the recorded balance is then misstated, and gains or losses on disposal may be wrong.
causes: No communication channel between operations (which disposes of assets) and finance (which maintains the register); disposals processed informally or by staff unaware of the accounting implications; scrapping and demolitions treated as non-events.
misstatement_scenario: Property, plant and equipment may be overstated by the net book value of assets that no longer exist. Gains or losses on disposal may be misstated or omitted. Depreciation may continue to be charged on assets that are gone.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with the volume of disposals, the number of sites, and the physical portability of assets. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; it is a control deficiency that creates the opportunity for overstatement, which the auditor must test for.

title: Unrecognised impairment losses
description: Where indicators of impairment exist but are not identified or evaluated, impairment losses may not be recognised and the carrying amount of assets may exceed their recoverable amount.
causes: No assigned responsibility for impairment reviews; management optimism or reluctance to recognise losses; indicators emerging gradually and going unnoticed; complex cash-generating unit structures that obscure underperformance.
misstatement_scenario: Carrying amounts may exceed recoverable amounts, overstating assets and profit. Required disclosures about impairment judgments and recognised losses may be omitted.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases where assets are exposed to technological change, market downturns or restructuring, and where cash-generating units are defined broadly enough to mask underperforming assets. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; no impairment may in fact be required, but that conclusion must be evidenced, not assumed.

title: Replaced significant components not derecognised
description: When a significant component of an asset is replaced, the carrying amount of the replaced part may remain in the asset's cost alongside the cost of the new part. The same economic capacity is then counted twice in the carrying amount.
causes: Maintenance information never reaching finance; replaced parts never separately identified in the register; work orders that describe the new work but not what was removed; focus on capitalising the new cost while overlooking derecognition.
misstatement_scenario: Property, plant and equipment may be overstated by the carrying amount of replaced components. Depreciation in future periods will be overstated. The existence assertion is affected for the replaced portion of the balance.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with the scale of replacement and overhaul programmes and where assets were never componentised. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; some replacements may be correctly treated, which the auditor verifies rather than assumes.

title: Invalid purchases recorded and paid for goods not received
description: Purchases may be recorded - and paid - for goods or services never received. This is a potential misstatement and a possible control deficiency; the factor does not prove any invoice was invalid.
causes: No matching of invoices to GRNs; weak segregation between ordering, receiving and payment approval; opportunity for fictitious invoices to be introduced.
misstatement_scenario: Purchases and trade payables overstated; cash lost through payments for goods not received; duplicate or fictitious supplier payments.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with purchase volumes, manual approval processes and weak segregation of duties. An unmatched invoice is an exception to investigate, not a confirmed misstatement. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Unrecorded liabilities and understated purchases at the reporting date
description: Goods received before year-end but invoiced afterward may be omitted from purchases and payables, understating liabilities. The factor describes a cut-off exposure; it does not prove any liability was omitted.
causes: Invoices arriving after the reporting date; no accrual for unmatched GRNs; purchases recorded by invoice date rather than receipt date.
misstatement_scenario: Trade payables and purchases understated; the subsequent period correspondingly overstated; incomplete liabilities affecting going-concern and covenant assessments.
inherent_risk_factors: Completeness of liabilities is inherently harder to test than existence, because the auditor looks for what is missing. The search for unrecorded liabilities is the standard response. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Payments to fictitious or altered suppliers; invalid payable balances
description: Uncontrolled changes to supplier master data may divert payments to fictitious suppliers or altered bank accounts, and may create invalid payable balances. The control weakness is the finding; whether any payment was actually diverted requires investigation.
causes: No independent approval of master changes; the same person maintains suppliers and processes payments; no periodic review of the supplier master.
misstatement_scenario: Cash misappropriated through diverted payments; purchases overstated with fictitious invoices; payable balances owed to non-existent suppliers.
inherent_risk_factors: This is both a control deficiency and a fraud opportunity. A change-log exception is a control deviation, not proof of fraud. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists or that fraud has occurred.

title: Duplicate recording of purchases and duplicate payments
description: The same supplier invoice may be recorded twice, overstating purchases and payables, and may be paid twice, causing a cash loss. Duplication is usually error, but the factor must be tested rather than assumed.
causes: No validation of invoice number uniqueness per supplier; invoices received through multiple channels; paid invoices not marked to prevent reprocessing.
misstatement_scenario: Purchases and payables overstated; duplicate cash payments; supplier credit balances requiring recovery.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with invoice volumes and decentralised processing. A duplicated invoice number is an exception requiring investigation - it may be a genuine reissued invoice from the supplier rather than a double recording. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Cut-off misstatement of purchases and trade payables
description: Purchases recorded in the wrong period misstate both purchases and payables at the reporting date. Cut-off errors can fall in either direction and are often error rather than fraud.
causes: Recording by invoice or processing date instead of receipt date; period-end processing backlogs; weak cut-off procedures.
misstatement_scenario: Purchases and payables misstated at the reporting date; distorted monthly trends; knock-on effects on inventory and cost of sales.
inherent_risk_factors: Cut-off testing in both directions is the standard response. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Revenue overstatement through premature recognition
description: Revenue may be recorded before the entity has satisfied the recognition criteria, so reported revenue and the related trade receivable are overstated for the period. This is a potential misstatement identified for audit attention - the factor indicates where the risk lies, not that revenue is in fact misstated.
causes: Billing driven by invoice date rather than delivery or performance; pressure to meet period-end targets; weak segregation between order processing, dispatch and billing; informal bill-and-hold practices; side agreements altering stated terms.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue and trade receivables overstated in the current period and understated in a later period; cut-off errors across periods; where deliberate, concealment through side agreements or backdated documents.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases where recognition criteria are complex or judgemental, where dispatch and billing systems are not integrated, and where management faces pressure to meet targets. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists; it identifies where the auditor should direct testing.

title: Revenue understatement through cut-off errors (late recording)
description: Sales earned before the reporting date may be omitted from the current period, understating revenue and trade receivables. The factor makes this possible; it does not prove any sale was actually omitted.
causes: Invoicing backlogs at period end; dispatch records not reconciled to the sales ledger; sales recorded by invoice date rather than by the recognition event.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue and receivables understated in the current period and overstated in the next; analytical expectations distorted; related tax liabilities understated.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases with period-end dispatch volumes and manual billing processes. Late recording is often error rather than fraud, but a systematic pattern warrants the same scepticism as premature recognition. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Fictitious or unsupported sales recorded in the ledger
description: Sales may be recorded that have no underlying economic event - fictitious invoices, or genuine invoices without the dispatch or performance that would make them valid revenue. Unsupported sales overstate revenue and receivables. The missing evidence is a control deficiency and a risk indicator, not proof that the sales are fictitious.
causes: Billing without matching dispatch evidence; weak segregation between billing and dispatch; dispatch documents not sequentially controlled; opportunity for staff to raise credit sales without authorisation.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue and trade receivables overstated; ageing receivables that will never be collected; in deliberate cases, concealment of misappropriated cash.
inherent_risk_factors: Risk increases where billing staff can raise invoices without independent dispatch confirmation and where credit control is weak. The absence of dispatch evidence for a sample item is an exception to investigate, not a confirmed misstatement. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.

title: Deliberate manipulation of revenue to achieve incentive targets
description: Where incentives depend on revenue targets, there is a fraud risk that revenue is deliberately misstated - pulled forward, deferred, inflated or fabricated - to trigger bonuses. This is a suspected fraud risk indicator only: most incentive schemes operate without misstatement, and the factor alone proves nothing.
causes: Material personal financial incentive tied to reported revenue; targets that are difficult to meet through genuine performance; weak governance oversight of revenue judgements; opportunity through manual journals or side agreements.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue misstated in either direction depending on the target mechanics; related receivables, cut-off and disclosures affected; concealment behaviours that also undermine other audit evidence.
inherent_risk_factors: Fraud risk factors are incentives and pressures, opportunities and rationalisations. Incentives alone do not create misstatement; the auditor assesses whether opportunity and rationalisation are also present. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists and does NOT establish fraud.

title: Material misstatement through unusual or non-routine year-end transactions
description: Unusual transactions recorded near year-end may lack commercial substance, be recorded in the wrong period, or be structured to achieve a desired accounting outcome. Each transaction must be understood on its own facts; unusual does not mean misstated.
causes: Desire to achieve period-end results; complex structures designed for an accounting outcome; transactions with related or unfamiliar parties on non-arm's length terms; weak authorisation of non-routine transactions.
misstatement_scenario: Revenue, receivables or related balances misstated; disclosures incomplete where the nature of the transactions is obscured; cut-off and classification errors.
inherent_risk_factors: Professional scepticism is essential: the auditor must understand the business rationale and obtain evidence of substance, not rely on management's description. The presence of this factor does NOT prove that a misstatement exists.
